speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction has persisted, and have you experienced easy bruising or other bleeding issues in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you have a personal history of prolonged bleeding after other dental procedures or minor cuts, and have you ever experienced spontaneous joint swelling or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help distinguish between different clotting factor deficiencies, do you recall if any of your previous joint swellings were painful and involved major joints like knees or elbows? Additionally, have you ever had bleeding from your nose or gums without any obvious injury?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to order some specific blood tests to check your clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Factor VIII assay, Factor IX assay

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT suggests a problem with the intrinsic coagulation pathway, likely involving Factor VIII or IX. Since the specific factor assays are unavailable, I will request a mixing study to determine if this is due to an inhibitor or a factor deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Mixing Study

speaker: Doctor
text: The correction of PTT in the mixing study confirms a clotting factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor. Given the male patient, prolonged PTT, and family history, I will request specific factor levels to distinguish between Hemophilia A and B. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII level, Factor IX level

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal factor levels are unexpected given the prolonged PTT and clinical history. I will request a ristocetin cofactor assay and von Willebrand factor antigen test to rule out von Willebrand disease. REQUEST TEST: Ristocetin cofactor assay, vWF antigen

text: The low ristocetin cofactor and vWF antigen levels confirm a diagnosis of von Willebrand disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: von Willebrand disease
